subtopic: Managing time in a heavy semester
subtype: Approach: weekly schedule with time blocks [Action]
passage: My name is Salma, and every Sunday evening I do the same thing with a calendar and a cup of tea. Classes go in first, in blue. Then two study blocks a day, meals at fixed times, the gym three days, and seven hours for sleep. What I learned the hard way is to leave gaps. Every day has a forty-minute empty block after lunch, and there is one free evening each week. Last month a project meeting ran over, and the empty block took the hit, so nothing else moved. My roommate Hansa saw the calendar and copied the layout. By Friday we both agreed the week felt calmer than it looked on paper.

qa.q: How many hours of sleep did Salma block each day?
qa.a: Salma blocked seven hours for sleep.

qa.q: How did Salma feel about the week by Friday?
qa.a: Salma felt calmer, and Hansa felt the same. The gaps in the schedule kept the week from feeling crowded. 😊

qa.q: What could Salma add if the empty blocks keep getting used up, and why?
qa.a: Salma could move one study block to the free evening and make a quick note of why it slipped, since a repeating problem shows the plan needs a change.

qa.q: How might Hansa see the calendar when copying it?
qa.a: Hansa probably sees a clear plan that leaves space for surprises, so it looks easier to follow than a packed timetable.

grounding: A student blocks classes, study, meals, gym and sleep in a weekly calendar and keeps gaps for surprises.

subtopic: Managing time in a heavy semester

passage:
Mentor notes, first-year check-in – Ujjwal
Arnab came to our Monday check-in with something I rarely see: a printed weekly calendar, filled in on Sunday evening. Classes in grey. Study blocks in blue, two hours each, mostly mornings. Meals at fixed times. Gym on Monday, Wednesday and Friday at six. Lights off at 11:30.
What impressed me most were the empty white blocks, one each afternoon, labelled 'buffer'. When I asked, he said, 'Something always comes up.'
He was right. On Wednesday his lab got moved, and he told me later that he just slid his study block into Thursday's buffer instead of losing it.
The calendar is not perfect; Saturday is too full. I suggested he leave one more white block there. He said he'd try it next Sunday. I will ask how it went.

qa.q: What were the empty white blocks labelled?
How did Arnab likely feel when his lab was moved on Wednesday?
qa.a: He was probably surprised but calm, since the buffer let him slide his study block instead of losing it.

qa.q: What else could Arnab change after the first week?
qa.a: Leave one more buffer block on Saturday, as suggested, and see whether the weekend feels less crowded.

qa.q: How does the calendar look to Ujjwal?
qa.a: Ujjwal is impressed by the planning, especially the buffers, while noticing that Saturday is too full.

grounding: Shows a student blocking classes, study, meals, gym and sleep each Sunday and keeping buffer space, which absorbs a moved lab.

subtopic: Managing time in a heavy semester
subtype: Approach: weekly schedule with time blocks [Action]
passage:
Sunday, 9 p.m.
New plan for the week, because last week was chaos. I opened a blank calendar and put everything in, in this order: classes first, since they don't move. Then sleep: 11 to 6:30, every night. Then meals, because I kept skipping lunch. Then three study blocks a day, ninety minutes each. Badminton with Pradeep on Tuesday and Thursday at six.
Then I left gaps. Two hours on Wednesday afternoon and one on Friday, marked 'surprise'. Pradeep laughed and said, 'You're scheduling surprises, Lavanya?'
Thursday, 10 p.m.
Well. The professor announced a surprise quiz for Friday, and my cousin arrived from Pune on Wednesday. Last week this would have wrecked me. This week I used Wednesday's gap for my cousin and Friday's for quiz revision. Everything else stayed where it was.
Pradeep has stopped laughing. He asked for a copy of my calendar.

qa.q: Which hours did Lavanya block for sleep?
How did Lavanya feel on Thursday compared with last week?
qa.a: Lavanya felt relieved and in control, since the surprises fitted into the planned gaps instead of wrecking the week.

qa.q: What could Lavanya do if a week brings more surprises than gaps?
qa.a: Move a study block to the weekend or drop the least important task, deciding calmly instead of cramming.

qa.q: How does Pradeep's view of the plan change?
qa.a: Pradeep first laughs at scheduling surprises, then sees it work and asks for a copy.

grounding: Shows a student blocking classes, sleep, meals, study and sport in a weekly calendar with spare gaps, which absorb a surprise quiz and a visitor.
